doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Swing at any tempo and Armstrong's Mills Brothers recordings
summary: Armstrong could swing with one note; Brunious recommends the Mills Brothers tracks, especially Nelly Gray, and calls for melody and time.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: A real musician, a jazz musician can swing at any tempo.

Any tempo. I mean Louis Armstrong could play one note and swing. I mean when you hear some of this stuff, Louis Armstrong singing, like with the Mills Brothers, just voices and a trumpet, and man did those guys swing. If you’ve never heard any of that stuff, get some of that. Unbelievable. There is one track on there that I mean comes to mind © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

immediately, “My Darling Nelly Gray.” And Louis sings a cadenza on the end that is unbelievable, it’s just so well paced, every zot, boop, bop and everything is just so well timed. It’s just, whooo. So we’re going to have to start really getting mature players to record. And you know we’ve got a lot of established players that are trying to play like — you know I claim I’m open minded so I’m going to play like the kids are playing, you know what I mean? [scats]. I don’t know, maybe that’s the wave, but I think we’re going to have to get back to melody and time.
